title: Reorder card on Home readout
headline: Extend. Ordering within 7 days rose 1.7 points, but the large-order guardrail is not yet safe.
summary: The share of returning customers who ordered within 7 days rose 1.7 points, from 33.4% to 35.1%, with a 95% interval of 0.8 to 2.6 points. The split was fine, and the test ran the full 14 days. Orders with 15 or more items fell 1.0 points, which equals the tolerance of 1.0 points, so the interval decides: it runs from a fall of 2.6 points to a rise of 0.6 points, and a harmful fall beyond the tolerance is not ruled out. Substitution complaints and cancellations held. The test could only reliably see a change of 1.3 points, which is more than the 1.0 point the team set, and the interval reaches below 1.0 point.
next: Run the test for 14 more days, keep the 50/50 split, and set the new end date to 2026-12-02.
Pull the counts only after every customer has had their 7 days, and read the test once, on that date.
Read the large-order guardrail again then. Ship only if its interval no longer reaches past the 1.0-point tolerance.
